title: Active Kit Subscriptions Per Month
prompt: Your at-home diagnostic test kit platform offers two subscription tiers: 'Basic' and 'Premium'. Each subscription has a created_date when the customer signed up and an ended_date when they cancelled (NULL if still active). You need to report, for every tier and every month from January 2024 through June 2024 inclusive, how many subscriptions were active at any point during that month. A subscription is considered active in a month if it was created by the end of the month AND either never ended OR ended on or after the first day of that month. Even if a tier had zero active subscriptions in a given month, that (tier, month) row must appear with a count of 0. Return three columns: tier (text), month_start (date), and active_count (integer). Order the results by tier ascending, then month_start ascending.
schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE subscription_tiers (tier_id INT PRIMARY KEY, tier_name TEXT NOT NULL); CREATE TABLE subscriptions (subscription_id INT PRIMARY KEY, tier_id INT NOT NULL REFERENCES subscription_tiers(tier_id), created_date DATE NOT NULL, ended_date DATE);

composite_moves: generate_series to build period spine (Jan-Jun 2024 monthly)
CROSS JOIN spine with subscription_tiers to create all (tier, month) cells
LEFT JOIN subscriptions with overlap predicate in ON clause: created_date < month_start + INTERVAL '1 month' AND (ended_date IS NULL OR ended_date >= month_start)
COUNT(subscription_id) to count active subscriptions per cell (0 for empty cells)
GROUP BY tier, month_start and ORDER BY tier, month_start

hints: You need to create every possible (tier, month) combination first, then attach subscription data to it so empty cells still appear.

Use generate_series to build a monthly spine from '2024-01-01' to '2024-06-01', CROSS JOIN it with subscription_tiers, then LEFT JOIN subscriptions with an overlap condition in the ON clause (not WHERE) that checks if the subscription was created before the month ended AND either never ended or ended on/after the month started.

The answer is: WITH months AS (SELECT generate_series(DATE '2024-01-01', DATE '2024-06-01', INTERVAL '1 month')::date AS month_start) SELECT t.tier_name AS tier, m.month_start, COUNT(s.subscription_id)::int AS active_count FROM months m CROSS JOIN subscription_tiers t LEFT JOIN subscriptions s ON s.tier_id = t.tier_id AND s.created_date < m.month_start + INTERVAL '1 month' AND (s.ended_date IS NULL OR s.ended_date >= m.month_start) GROUP BY t.tier_name, m.month_start ORDER BY t.tier_name, m.month_start;
answer_key:
WITH months AS (
  SELECT generate_series(DATE '2024-01-01', DATE '2024-06-01', INTERVAL '1 month')::date AS month_start
)
SELECT
  t.tier_name AS tier,
  m.month_start,
  COUNT(s.subscription_id)::int AS active_count
FROM months m
CROSS JOIN subscription_tiers t
LEFT JOIN subscriptions s
  ON s.tier_id = t.tier_id
 AND s.created_date < m.month_start + INTERVAL '1 month'
 AND (s.ended_date IS NULL OR s.ended_date >= m.month_start)
GROUP BY t.tier_name, m.month_start
ORDER BY t.tier_name, m.month_start;

_meta.scenario: an at-home diagnostic test kit platform tracking kit shipped and results released
